message: The effect now depends on summaryIndex so it fires once, but no test navigates away from Summary (or changes language) and checks the reader stays put. Reverting to the handleStepChange dependency keeps every test green.
Gating the Confirmation on !readOnly closes the submit dialog and its spinner as soon as the mutation succeeds, while handleSubmit is still applying the location, toasting, and redirecting.
The effect deps change from handleStepChange to summaryIndex has no regression test, so the snap-back to Summary can return unnoticed.
The new !readOnly gate on the Confirmation has no test, so reverting it leaves every test green.
Moving to Summary in a useEffect lets step 1 mount and query for one commit on a fresh load of a submitted questionnaire.
dismissalDetail: same as #9: one render on step 1 before the jump, its queries are shared and cached

message: The read-only effect calls setCurrentIndex(summaryIndex) with no -1 guard, unlike handleStepChange. If steps ever lack Summary, currentStep becomes undefined and the page blanks.
dismissalDetail: useSteps always includes the Summary step, so summaryIndex is never -1

message: No test covers a failed CompleteNewStaffQuestionnaire asserting the success toast does not appear.
dismissalDetail: the failed-submit path is unchanged by this PR; Confirmation already keeps the dialog open on an error

message: handleSubmit still shows the success toast and redirects even when completeQuestionnaire silently no-ops on a read-only questionnaire.
The loading guard was removed but the diff adds no test for the in-flight query state, so a flash of hidden or shown nav during loading is unpinned.
dismissalDetail: behavior is unchanged: with no data the item stays hidden, the same as the old loading check, and the existing tests cover it

message: summaryIndex repeats handleStepChange's findIndex lookup to dodge the steps array changing identity whenever t changes.
dismissalDetail: a number dependency keeps the effect from re-firing when steps changes identity on a language change, which the new test pins

message: The comment explaining why a cache-and-network refetch must not hide the nav item was dropped along with the redundant loading check.
